nodes.title: Morphisms with constant second component factor through a slice
nodes.statement:
Let \(T\), \(X\), \(Y\) be objects of \(\mathcal C\), let \(y\) be a point of \(Y\), and
  let \(p : T \to X \times Y\) be a morphism whose second component is constant with value
  \(y\), i.e.\ \(\mathrm{pr}_2 \circ p = y \circ t_T\). Then
  \[
    p \;=\; \sigma_y \circ (\mathrm{pr}_1 \circ p).
  \]

nodes.title: Transfer of slice constancy
nodes.statement:
In the situation of \ref{lem:slice_factorisation}, let moreover \(f : X \times Y \to Z\) be
  a morphism which is constant on the slice over \(y\), with value a point \(c\) of \(Z\):
  \(f \circ \sigma_y = c \circ t_X\). Then
  \[
    f \circ p \;=\; c \circ t_T .
  \]

nodes.title: Constancy
nodes.statement:
Let \(R\) be a commutative ring and \(s_V : V \to \Spec R\) a morphism of schemes inducing
  an isomorphism \(\Gamma(\Spec R, \struct{\Spec R}) \to \Gamma(V, \struct V)\) on global
  sections. Let \(q : V \to W\) be a morphism of schemes whose set-theoretic image is
  contained in an affine open \(U \subseteq W\). Then \(q\) is \emph{constant}: there is a
  morphism \(z : \Spec R \to W\) with \(q = z \circ s_V\).

nodes.title: Constancy, relative form
nodes.statement:
Let \(R\) be a commutative ring and let \(V\), \(W\) be schemes over \(\Spec R\), with
  structure morphisms \(v\), \(w\), such that \(v\) induces an isomorphism on global
  sections. Let \(q : V \to W\) be a morphism over \(\Spec R\) whose set-theoretic image is
  contained in an affine open \(U \subseteq W\). Then there is a \emph{point}
  \(c : \Spec R \to W\) over \(\Spec R\) (a section of \(w\)) with \(q = c \circ v\).

nodes.title: Points are determined by their underlying points
nodes.statement:
Let \(T\) be a scheme locally of finite type over the algebraically closed field \(K\), and
  let \(p, q : \Spec K \to T\) be two points of \(T\) over \(K\). If \(p\) and \(q\) send the
  unique point \(*\) of \(\Spec K\) to the same point of the topological space of \(T\), then
  \(p = q\).

nodes.title: Products of geometrically integral schemes are integral
nodes.statement:
Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be schemes over a field \(k\), each geometrically integral and locally
  of finite type over \(k\). Then the product \(X \times_k Y\) is an integral scheme.

nodes.title: Rigidity
nodes.statement:
Let \(K\) be an algebraically closed field and let \(X\), \(Y\), \(Z\) be schemes over
  \(K\) such that
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item \(X\) is proper and geometrically integral over \(K\);
    \item \(Y\) is locally of finite type over \(K\) and the product \(X \times_K Y\) is an
      integral scheme (automatic when \(Y\) is also geometrically integral, by
      \ref{lem:product_integral});
    \item \(Z\) is separated and locally of finite type over \(K\).
  \end{enumerate}
  Let \(f : X \times_K Y \to Z\) be a morphism over \(K\), let \(y_0\) be a point of \(Y\)
  and \(z_0\) a point of \(Z\), and suppose \(f\) contracts the slice over \(y_0\) to
  \(z_0\):
  \[
    f \circ \sigma_{y_0} \;=\; z_0 \circ t_X .
  \]
  Then there is a \emph{unique} morphism \(g : Y \to Z\) over \(K\) with
  \(f = g \circ \mathrm{pr}_2\).

nodes.title: Pointed morphisms are homomorphisms
nodes.statement:
Let \(K\) be an algebraically closed field, let \(A\) be a monoid scheme over \(K\) which
  is proper and geometrically integral over \(K\), and let \(B\) be a group scheme over
  \(K\) which is separated and locally of finite type over \(K\). Then every morphism
  \(g : A \to B\) over \(K\) with \(g \circ e_A = e_B\) is a homomorphism of monoid schemes.

nodes.title: Stability under nonnegative powers of \(T\)
nodes.statement:
Let \(Q \subseteq N\) be a \(k\)-submodule such that \(T \cdot x \in Q\) for every
  \(x \in Q\). Then for every \(x \in Q\) and every integer \(m \ge 0\), \(T^m \cdot x \in Q\).

nodes.title: Stability under nonnegative powers of \(T^{-1}\)
nodes.statement:
Let \(Q \subseteq N\) be a \(k\)-submodule such that \(T^{-1} \cdot x \in Q\) for every
  \(x \in Q\). Then for every \(x \in Q\) and every integer \(m \ge 0\),
  \(T^{-m} \cdot x \in Q\).

nodes.title: Two-lattice finiteness, spanning-set form
Two-lattice finiteness, localization form
Two-lattice finiteness, localization form via powers of the generator
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\), \(N\), \(Q_0\), \(Q_1\) be as in Corollary~\ref{cor:two_lattice_loc}, satisfying
  hypotheses (1) and (2) there, and suppose in place of (3) and (4) that:
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item[(3a)] every \(n \in N\) satisfies: there is an integer \(m \ge 0\) with
      \(T^m \cdot n \in Q_0\), where \(T^m\) denotes the ordinary \(m\)-th power of the ring
      element \(T \in k[T,T^{-1}]\);
    \item[(4a)] every \(n \in N\) satisfies: there is an integer \(m \ge 0\) with
      \(T^{-m} \cdot n \in Q_1\), where \(T^{-m}\) denotes the ordinary \(m\)-th power of
      \(T^{-1} \in k[T,T^{-1}]\).
  \end{enumerate}
  Then \(N / (Q_0 + Q_1)\) is a finite \(k\)-module.

nodes.title: Category of curves
nodes.statement:
Let \(\mathrm{Curve}(k)\) denote the category whose objects are smooth proper geometrically
  irreducible curves over \(k\) and whose morphisms are morphisms of \(k\)-schemes.

nodes.title: Jacobian functor
nodes.statement:
The Jacobian is a contravariant functor
  \[
    \Jac : \mathrm{Curve}(k)^{\op} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Grp}\bigl(\Over(\Spec k)\bigr),
  \]
  sending a curve to its Jacobian group scheme and a morphism of curves to the induced pullback of
  line bundles. In particular an isomorphism of curves induces an isomorphism of Jacobian group
  schemes.

nodes.title: Base change of schemes
nodes.statement:
For a field extension \(k \to L\), base change is the functor
  \(X \mapsto X \times_{\Spec k} \Spec L\) from \(k\)-schemes to \(L\)-schemes.

nodes.title: Jacobians commute with base change
nodes.statement:
For every field extension \(k \to L\) and every curve \(C\) over \(k\) there is a canonical
  isomorphism of group schemes over \(L\)
  \[
    \Jac(C)_L \;\cong\; \Jac(C_L).
  \]

nodes.title: Identity coherence
nodes.statement:
The base-change isomorphism for the trivial extension \(k \to k\) is the identity, compatibly with
  the identification \(C_k \cong C\).

nodes.title: Cocycle coherence
nodes.statement:
For a tower \(k \to L \to M\) the base-change isomorphisms compose: the isomorphism for \(k \to M\)
  agrees with base-changing the isomorphism for \(k \to L\) along \(L \to M\) and then applying the
  isomorphism for \(L \to M\), compatibly with the identification \((C_L)_M \cong C_M\).

nodes.title: Compatibility with the Abel--Jacobi map
nodes.statement:
Base change carries the Abel--Jacobi map of \((C, P)\) to the Abel--Jacobi map of \((C_L, P_L)\):
  under \(\Jac(C)_L \cong \Jac(C_L)\), the base change of \(\varphi_P\) is \(\varphi_{P_L}\).

nodes.title: Genus
nodes.statement:
The \emph{genus} of a smooth proper curve \(C\) over \(k\) is
  \[
    g(C) \;=\; \dim_k H^1\!\bigl(C, \struct C\bigr),
  \]
  the \(k\)-dimension of the first cohomology group of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf
  of \(k\)-modules on the small Zariski site of \(C\) (Definition~\ref{def:moduleKSheaf}),
  with cohomology the \(\Ext\)-groups from the constant sheaf
  (Definition~\ref{def:HModule}).

nodes.title: Jacobian
nodes.statement:
The \emph{Jacobian} \(\Jac(C)\) of a smooth proper curve \(C\) over \(k\) is the identity
  component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) of the relative Picard scheme of \(C\) over \(k\): the \(k\)-scheme
  representing (the fppf-sheafification of) the functor of degree-zero line bundles on \(C\).

nodes.title: Group scheme structure
nodes.statement:
\(\Jac(C)\) is a commutative group scheme over \(k\), with multiplication induced by the tensor
  product of line bundles.

nodes.title: Smoothness of the Jacobian
nodes.statement: \(\Jac(C)\) is smooth over \(k\) of relative dimension \(g(C)\).

nodes.title: Properness of the Jacobian
nodes.statement: \(\Jac(C)\) is proper over \(k\).

nodes.title: Geometric irreducibility of the Jacobian
nodes.statement: \(\Jac(C)\) is geometrically irreducible over \(k\).

nodes.title: Abel--Jacobi map
Base point maps to the origin
nodes.statement:
The Abel--Jacobi map \(\varphi_P\) sends the base point \(P\) to the neutral element of
  \(\Jac(C)\): \(\varphi_P \circ P = 0\).

nodes.title: Universal property of the Jacobian
nodes.statement:
\(\Jac(C)\) is the Albanese variety of \(C\): for every abelian variety \(A\) over \(k\) and every
  morphism \(f : C \to A\) with \(f \circ P = 0\), there is a unique homomorphism of group schemes
  \(g : \Jac(C) \to A\) such that \(f = g \circ \varphi_P\).

nodes.title: The constant sheaf
nodes.statement:
The constant sheaf \(R_J\) of \(R\)-modules on \((\mathcal C, J)\) with value \(R\): the
  sheafification of the constant presheaf with value \(R\).

nodes.title: Sheaf cohomology
nodes.statement:
For a sheaf \(F\) of \(R\)-modules on \((\mathcal C, J)\) and \(n \ge 0\), the degree-\(n\)
  cohomology of \(F\) is the \(R\)-module
  \[
    H^n(F) \;=\; \Ext^n\bigl(R_J,\, F\bigr),
  \]
  the \(\Ext\)-group computed in the category of sheaves of \(R\)-modules.

nodes.title: Functoriality
nodes.statement:
A morphism of sheaves \(f : F \to G\) induces an \(R\)-linear map
  \(H^n(F) \to H^n(G)\) for every \(n\), by covariant functoriality of \(\Ext\) in the second
  argument. The identity induces the identity, and a composite induces the composite.

nodes.title: No higher cohomology on injectives
nodes.statement:
If \(F\) is an injective object of the category of sheaves of \(R\)-modules, then
  \(H^{n+1}(F) = 0\) for every \(n \ge 0\).

nodes.title: The adjunction, linearly
nodes.statement:
Assume the category \(\mathcal C\) has a terminal object \(\top\). For every \(R\)-module
  \(M\) and every sheaf \(F\) of \(R\)-modules there is an \(R\)-linear equivalence
  \[
    \Hom\bigl(\underline{M},\, F\bigr) \;\cong\; \Hom_R\bigl(M,\, F(\top)\bigr),
  \]
  where \(\underline{M}\) denotes the constant sheaf with value \(M\); it is the hom-bijection
  of the adjunction between the constant-sheaf functor and evaluation at \(\top\).

nodes.title: Morphisms out of the constant sheaf are sections
nodes.statement:
The \(R\)-linear equivalence
  \(\Hom(R_J, F) \cong F(\top)\): specialize \ref{def:constAdjHomEquiv} to \(M = R\) and
  compose with the canonical evaluation \(\Hom_R(R, N) \cong N\), \(u \mapsto u(1)\).

nodes.title: Naturality
nodes.statement:
The equivalence of \ref{def:constHomEquiv} is natural in the sheaf: for
  \(\varphi : R_J \to F\) and \(f : F \to G\), the section corresponding to
  \(f \circ \varphi\) is \(f_\top\) applied to the section corresponding to \(\varphi\).

nodes.title: Degree-zero cohomology is global sections
nodes.statement:
The \(R\)-linear equivalence \(H^0(F) \cong F(\top)\): the canonical identification
  \(\Ext^0(R_J, F) \cong \Hom(R_J, F)\) followed by \ref{def:constHomEquiv}.

nodes.title: Naturality in degree zero
nodes.statement:
The equivalence \(H^0(F) \cong F(\top)\) of \ref{def:HModule_linearEquiv0} is natural: for
  \(f : F \to G\), applying \(f_\top\) to the section corresponding to \(x \in H^0(F)\)
  yields the section corresponding to the image of \(x\) under \(H^0(f)\).

nodes.title: The free sheaf of \(R\)-modules on an object of the site
nodes.statement:
For an object \(U\) of \(\mathcal C\), the free sheaf of \(R\)-modules on \(U\), written
  \(R[U]\): the sheafification of the presheaf \(V \mapsto\) the free \(R\)-module on the
  set \(\Hom(V, U)\), with restriction maps induced by precomposition.

nodes.title: Functoriality in the object of the site
nodes.statement:
A morphism \(i : U \to V\) of \(\mathcal C\) induces a morphism of sheaves of
  \(R\)-modules \(R[i] : R[U] \to R[V]\): apply the free-\(R\)-module-on-a-set functor and
  sheafification to the induced map of representable presheaves
  \(\Hom(-,U) \to \Hom(-,V)\), \(g \mapsto i \circ g\).

nodes.title: Free sheaves of modules represent sections
nodes.statement:
For every object \(U\) of \(\mathcal C\) and every sheaf \(F\) of \(R\)-modules, an
  \(R\)-linear equivalence
  \[
    \Hom\bigl(R[U],\, F\bigr) \;\cong\; F(U).
  \]

nodes.title: Naturality of the section equivalence
Cohomology of an object of the site
nodes.statement:
For an object \(U\) of \(\mathcal C\), a sheaf \(F\) of \(R\)-modules and \(n \ge 0\), the
  degree-\(n\) cohomology of \(U\) with coefficients in \(F\) is the \(R\)-module
  \[
    H'^n(U, F) \;=\; \Ext^n\bigl(R[U],\, F\bigr).
  \]

nodes.title: Degree zero is sections
nodes.statement:
The \(R\)-linear equivalence \(H'^0(U, F) \cong F(U)\): the canonical identification
  \(\Ext^0(R[U], F) \cong \Hom(R[U], F)\) followed by \ref{def:freeModuleSheafHomEquiv}.

nodes.title: Restriction
nodes.statement:
For \(i : U \to V\) in \(\mathcal C\), restriction along \(i\) is the \(R\)-linear map
  \(H'^n(V, F) \to H'^n(U, F)\), \(x \mapsto x \circ R[i]\): precomposition with
  \(R[i] : R[U] \to R[V]\) (contravariant functoriality of \(\Ext^n(-, F)\)).

nodes.title: The free sheaf on a terminal object is the constant sheaf
nodes.statement:
If \(T\) is a terminal object of \(\mathcal C\), a canonical isomorphism of sheaves of
  \(R\)-modules \(R[T] \cong R_J\).

nodes.title: Cohomology of the site is cohomology of a terminal object
nodes.statement:
For \(T\) terminal in \(\mathcal C\) and every \(n\), an \(R\)-linear equivalence
  \(H^n(F) \cong H'^n(T, F)\).

nodes.title: The algebra map on sections
nodes.statement:
For every open \(U \subseteq X\), the canonical ring homomorphism \(k \to \Gamma(X, U)\):
  the map induced on global sections by the structure morphism, followed by restriction to
  \(U\). It commutes with the restriction maps of the structure sheaf; in particular each
  \(\Gamma(X, U)\) is a \(k\)-algebra --- hence a \(k\)-module --- and all restriction maps
  are \(k\)-linear.

nodes.title: The structure sheaf as a sheaf of \(k\)-modules
nodes.statement:
The structure sheaf of \(X\), viewed as a sheaf \(\struct{X/k}\) of \(k\)-modules on the
  small Zariski site of \(X\): its sections over an open \(U\) are \(\Gamma(X, U)\) with the
  \(k\)-module structure of \ref{def:overAlgebraMap}, and its restriction maps are those of
  the structure sheaf.

nodes.title: Degree-zero cohomology of the structure sheaf
nodes.statement: The \(k\)-linear equivalence \(H^0\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr) \cong \Gamma(X, \struct X)\).

nodes.title: Denominator clearing on an affine open
nodes.statement:
Let \(X\) be a scheme, \(U \subseteq X\) an affine open, \(V \subseteq X\) an open with
  \(U \subseteq V\), and \(g \in \Gamma(X, V)\) a section of the structure sheaf on \(V\) (so
  that \(D(g) \subseteq V\) is its basic open). For every \(c \in \Gamma(X, U \cap D(g))\)
  there exist \(N \ge 0\) and \(e \in \Gamma(X, U)\) such that
  \[
    e|_{U \cap D(g)} \;=\; \bigl(g|_{U}\bigr)|_{U \cap D(g)}^{N} \cdot c .
  \]

nodes.title: Annihilation on an affine open
nodes.statement:
Let \(X\) be a scheme, \(U \subseteq X\) an affine open, \(V \subseteq X\) an open with
  \(U \subseteq V\), and \(g \in \Gamma(X, V)\) a section of the structure sheaf on \(V\) (so
  that \(D(g) \subseteq V\) is its basic open). If \(t \in \Gamma(X, U)\) restricts to zero
  on \(U \cap D(g)\), then \((g|_U)^{M} \cdot t = 0\) in \(\Gamma(X, U)\) for some \(M \ge 0\).

nodes.title: Degree-one \v{C}ech cobounding on an affine open
nodes.statement:
Let \(X\) be a scheme and \(U\) an affine open of \(X\). Let \(f_1, \dots, f_n \in
  \Gamma(X, U)\) with \(D(f_1) \cup \dots \cup D(f_n) = U\). Let
  \(a_{ij} \in \Gamma\bigl(X, D(f_i) \cap D(f_j)\bigr)\) be a \v{C}ech \(1\)-cocycle: for all
  \(i, j, l\),
  \[
    a_{il} \;=\; a_{ij} + a_{jl}
    \qquad \text{on } D(f_i) \cap D(f_j) \cap D(f_l).
  \]
  Then there are sections \(b_i \in \Gamma\bigl(X, D(f_i)\bigr)\) with
  \[
    a_{ij} \;=\; b_i - b_j \qquad \text{on } D(f_i) \cap D(f_j)
  \]
  for all \(i, j\).

nodes.title: Degree-one \v{C}ech cobounding on an affine scheme
nodes.statement:
Let \(X\) be an affine scheme and let \(f_1, \dots, f_n\) be global sections of the
  structure sheaf with \(D(f_1) \cup \dots \cup D(f_n) = X\). Let
  \(a_{ij} \in \Gamma\bigl(X, D(f_i) \cap D(f_j)\bigr)\) be a \v{C}ech \(1\)-cocycle as in
  \ref{thm:affine_open_cech_cobounding}. Then there are sections
  \(b_i \in \Gamma\bigl(X, D(f_i)\bigr)\) with \(a_{ij} = b_i - b_j\) on
  \(D(f_i) \cap D(f_j)\) for all \(i, j\).

nodes.title: A vanishing criterion for \(\Ext^1\)
nodes.statement:
Let \(\mathcal A\) be an abelian category (with \(\Ext\)-groups), let
  \(\iota : A \to I\) be a monomorphism with \(I\) injective, and let \(L\) be an object. If
  every morphism \(L \to \coker \iota\) lifts along the projection
  \(\pi : I \to \coker \iota\), then \(\Ext^1(L, A) = 0\).

nodes.title: Sections are left exact
nodes.statement:
Let \(\iota : F \to G\) be a monomorphism of sheaves of \(R\)-modules on a site and let
  \(U\) be an object of the site. If \(c \in G(U)\) maps to zero in \((\coker \iota)(U)\),
  then \(c = \iota_U(a)\) for a (unique) \(a \in F(U)\).

nodes.title: Monomorphisms are injective on sections
nodes.statement:
A monomorphism of sheaves of \(R\)-modules on a site is injective on sections over every
  object of the site.

nodes.title: Sections surjectivity on an affine open
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a commutative ring, \(X\) a scheme over \(\Spec k\), \(U\) an affine open of
  \(X\), \(G\) a sheaf of \(k\)-modules on the small Zariski site of \(X\), and
  \(\iota : \struct{X/k} \to G\) a monomorphism. Then every section of
  \(\coker \iota\) over \(U\) lifts to a section of \(G\) over \(U\): the map
  \(G(U) \to (\coker \iota)(U)\) is surjective.

nodes.title: Vanishing of \(H^1{}'\) on affine opens
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a commutative ring, \(X\) a scheme over \(\Spec k\) and \(U\) an affine open
  of \(X\). Then
  \[
    H'^1\bigl(U, \struct{X/k}\bigr) \;=\; 0 .
  \]
  No hypothesis on \(X\) beyond the affineness of \(U\) is needed.

nodes.title: Vanishing of \(H^1\) on affine schemes
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a commutative ring and \(X\) an affine scheme over \(\Spec k\). Then
  \[
    H^1\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr) \;=\; 0 .
  \]

nodes.title: Mayer--Vietoris square
nodes.statement:
\textit{Provided by Mathlib.}
  Let \((\mathcal C, J)\) be a small site. A Mayer--Vietoris square consists of four objects
  \(X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4\) of \(\mathcal C\) and morphisms \(f_{12} : X_1 \to X_2\),
  \(f_{13} : X_1 \to X_3\), \(f_{24} : X_2 \to X_4\), \(f_{34} : X_3 \to X_4\) such that the
  two composites \(X_1 \to X_2 \to X_4\) and \(X_1 \to X_3 \to X_4\) agree, \(f_{13}\) is a
  monomorphism, and, after applying the representable-presheaf-then-sheafification functor
  \(\mathcal C \to \mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C, J; \mathrm{Set})\), the resulting square of
  sheaves of sets is a pushout square: the image of \(X_4\) is the pushout, over the image of
  \(X_1\), of the images of \(X_2\) and \(X_3\). The prototypical example is
  \(X_1 = U \cap V\), \(X_2 = U\), \(X_3 = V\), \(X_4 = U \cup V\) for two opens \(U, V\) of a
  topological space, with the evident inclusions.

nodes.title: The sheaf condition of a Mayer--Vietoris square
nodes.statement:
\textit{Provided by Mathlib.}
  Let \(S = (X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4,f_{12},f_{13},f_{24},f_{34})\) be a Mayer--Vietoris square on
  \((\mathcal C, J)\) and let \(P\) be a presheaf on \(\mathcal C\). Say \(P\) satisfies the
  sheaf condition for \(S\) when the square \(P(X_4) \to P(X_2) \to P(X_1)\),
  \(P(X_4) \to P(X_3) \to P(X_1)\) (restriction along \(f_{24}, f_{12}\) and along
  \(f_{34}, f_{13}\)) is a pullback square: equivalently, restriction identifies \(P(X_4)\)
  with the pairs \((u,v) \in P(X_2) \times P(X_3)\) of equal restriction to \(X_1\). Every
  sheaf satisfies the sheaf condition for every Mayer--Vietoris square of its site.

nodes.title: The Mayer--Vietoris short complex of free sheaves
nodes.statement:
For a Mayer--Vietoris square \(S\) on \((\mathcal C, J)\), the complex of sheaves of
  \(R\)-modules
  \[
    R[X_1] \xrightarrow{\ (R[f_{12}],\, -R[f_{13}])\ } R[X_2] \oplus R[X_3]
      \xrightarrow{\ R[f_{24}] + R[f_{34}]\ } R[X_4],
  \]
  whose composite is zero by the commutativity of \(S\)'s square.

nodes.title: The Mayer--Vietoris short complex is short exact
nodes.statement:
For every Mayer--Vietoris square \(S\), the complex of \ref{def:moduleShortComplex} is a
  short exact sequence of sheaves of \(R\)-modules:
  \[
    0 \to R[X_1] \to R[X_2] \oplus R[X_3] \to R[X_4] \to 0 .
  \]

nodes.title: The restriction-difference map
nodes.statement:
For a Mayer--Vietoris square \(S\) and a sheaf \(F\) of \(R\)-modules, the \(R\)-linear map
  \[
    F(X_2) \times F(X_3) \longrightarrow F(X_1), \qquad
    (s_2, s_3) \longmapsto s_2|_{X_1} - s_3|_{X_1},
  \]
  restricting along \(f_{12}\) and \(f_{13}\) respectively and taking the difference.

nodes.title: Degree-zero exactness
nodes.statement:
For a Mayer--Vietoris square \(S\) and a sheaf \(F\) of \(R\)-modules, the sequence
  \[
    0 \to F(X_4) \xrightarrow{\ (\mathrm{res},\,\mathrm{res})\ } F(X_2) \times F(X_3)
      \xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{moduleDiff}\ } F(X_1)
  \]
  is exact: the pair of restrictions to \(X_2, X_3\) is injective, and its image is exactly
  the kernel of \ref{def:moduleDiff}.

nodes.title: Contravariant long exact sequence of \(\Ext\)
nodes.statement:
\textit{Provided by Mathlib.}
  Let \(0 \to A \xrightarrow{f} B \xrightarrow{g} C \to 0\) be a short exact sequence in an
  abelian category with \(\Ext\)-groups and let \(Y\) be any object. There is a canonical
  extension class \(\delta \in \Ext^1(C, A)\) (built from the connecting homomorphism of the
  sequence), and for every \(n \ge 0\) the sequence of abelian groups
  \[
    \Ext^n(C,Y) \xrightarrow{g^*} \Ext^n(B,Y) \xrightarrow{f^*} \Ext^n(A,Y)
      \xrightarrow{\ \delta \cdot (-)\ } \Ext^{n+1}(C,Y) \xrightarrow{g^*} \Ext^{n+1}(B,Y)
      \xrightarrow{f^*} \Ext^{n+1}(A,Y)
  \]
  is exact at each of the four inner terms, where \(f^*, g^*\) are precomposition
  (contravariant functoriality of \(\Ext(-,Y)\)) and \(\delta \cdot (-)\) is composition
  (Yoneda product) with \(\delta\). (Convention: \(\Ext^0 = \Hom\).) If \(B = X_2 \oplus X_3\)
  is a direct sum, \(\Ext^n(B,Y) \cong \Ext^n(X_2,Y) \times \Ext^n(X_3,Y)\) naturally,
  compatibly with \(f^*, g^*\).

nodes.title: The connecting map
nodes.statement:
For a Mayer--Vietoris square \(S\) and a sheaf \(F\) of \(R\)-modules, the connecting map
  \(F(X_1) \to H'^1(X_4, F)\): the identification
  \(F(X_1) \cong H'^0(X_1,F) = \Ext^0(R[X_1], F)\) of \ref{def:HModule'_linearEquiv0},
  followed by the map \(\delta \cdot (-) : \Ext^0(R[X_1],F) \to \Ext^1(R[X_4],F) = H'^1(X_4,F)\)
  of \ref{lem:ext_contravariant_les} for the short exact sequence of
  \ref{thm:moduleShortComplex_shortExact} (\(A = R[X_1]\), \(B = R[X_2] \oplus R[X_3]\),
  \(C = R[X_4]\)).

nodes.title: Exactness at \(F(X_1)\)
nodes.statement:
For a Mayer--Vietoris square \(S\) and a sheaf \(F\) of \(R\)-modules,
  \(\ker(\mathrm{moduleDelta}) = \mathrm{range}(\mathrm{moduleDiff})\) as submodules of
  \(F(X_1)\): the connecting class of a difference of restrictions vanishes, and conversely
  every section of \(F(X_1)\) with vanishing connecting class is such a difference.

nodes.title: Exactness at \(H'^1(X_4,F)\)
nodes.statement:
For a Mayer--Vietoris square \(S\) and a sheaf \(F\) of \(R\)-modules,
  \(\ker(\mathrm{res}_{f_{24}}) \cap \ker(\mathrm{res}_{f_{34}}) = \mathrm{range}(\mathrm{moduleDelta})\)
  as submodules of \(H'^1(X_4,F)\), where
  \(\mathrm{res}_{f_{24}}, \mathrm{res}_{f_{34}} : H'^1(X_4,F) \to H'^1(X_2,F), H'^1(X_3,F)\)
  are the restrictions of \ref{def:HModule'_res}: the connecting class of any section of
  \(F(X_1)\) restricts to zero on both \(X_2\) and \(X_3\), and conversely every class
  restricting to zero on both is a connecting class.

nodes.title: Surjectivity of the connecting map
nodes.statement:
If \(H'^1(X_2,F)\) and \(H'^1(X_3,F)\) are both zero, then
  \(\mathrm{moduleDelta} : F(X_1) \to H'^1(X_4,F)\) is surjective.

nodes.title: The connecting map on the cokernel
nodes.statement:
Since \(\mathrm{range}(\mathrm{moduleDiff}) \subseteq \ker(\mathrm{moduleDelta})\)
  (\ref{lem:mv_exact_at_X1}), \(\mathrm{moduleDelta}\) descends to an \(R\)-linear map
  \[
    F(X_1)/\mathrm{range}(\mathrm{moduleDiff}) \longrightarrow H'^1(X_4,F).
  \]

nodes.title: The Mayer--Vietoris two-cover cokernel computation
nodes.statement:
If \(H'^1(X_2,F)\) and \(H'^1(X_3,F)\) are both zero, the map of
  \ref{def:moduleDeltaQuotient} is an \(R\)-linear isomorphism
  \[
    F(X_1)/\mathrm{range}(\mathrm{moduleDiff}) \;\cong\; H'^1(X_4,F).
  \]

nodes.title: Compatibility with the connecting map
nodes.statement:
Under the isomorphism of \ref{thm:h1LinearEquiv}, the class of \(s \in F(X_1)\)
  corresponds to \(\mathrm{moduleDelta}(s)\).

nodes.title: Mayer--Vietoris square of two opens
nodes.statement:
\textit{Provided by Mathlib.}
  For a topological space \(T\) and opens \(X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4 \subseteq T\) with
  \(X_1 = X_2 \cap X_3\) and \(X_4 = X_2 \cup X_3\), the square \((X_1,X_2,X_3,X_4)\) with the
  inclusion morphisms is a Mayer--Vietoris square (Definition~\ref{def:MayerVietorisSquare})
  on the small Zariski site of \(T\).

nodes.title: The two-cover square
nodes.statement:
For a scheme \(X\) and opens \(U_0, U_1 \subseteq X\) with \(U_0 \cup U_1 = X\), the
  Mayer--Vietoris square \((U_0 \cap U_1,\, U_0,\, U_1,\, X)\) on the small Zariski site of
  \(X\) (Definition~\ref{def:opens_mayerVietorisSquare'}, specialized to \(X_4 = X\)), with
  the inclusion morphisms.

nodes.title: The two-cover \(H^1\) computation, general coefficients
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a commutative ring, \(X\) a scheme over \(\Spec k\), \(U_0, U_1 \subseteq X\)
  opens with \(U_0 \cup U_1 = X\), and \(F\) a sheaf of \(k\)-modules on the small Zariski
  site of \(X\) with \(H'^1(U_0,F) = H'^1(U_1,F) = 0\). Then
  \[
    H^1(X,F) \;\cong\;
      F(U_0 \cap U_1) \big/ \mathrm{range}\bigl((s_0,s_1) \mapsto
        s_0|_{U_0 \cap U_1} - s_1|_{U_0 \cap U_1}\bigr) .
  \]

nodes.title: The two-cover restriction-difference map
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a commutative ring, \(X\) a scheme over \(\Spec k\), and \(U_0, U_1 \subseteq X\)
  opens. The \(k\)-linear map
  \[
    \Gamma(X,U_0) \times \Gamma(X,U_1) \longrightarrow \Gamma(X, U_0 \cap U_1), \qquad
    (s_0,s_1) \longmapsto s_0|_{U_0 \cap U_1} - s_1|_{U_0 \cap U_1} .
  \]
  When \(U_0 \cup U_1 = X\), this is the map \ref{def:moduleDiff} of the two-cover square
  (Definition~\ref{def:twoCoverSquare}) for the structure sheaf \(\struct{X/k}\).

nodes.title: The two-cover cokernel carrier
nodes.statement:
The \(k\)-module \(\Gamma(X, U_0 \cap U_1)/\mathrm{range}(\mathrm{diff})\), the cokernel of
  the map of \ref{def:TwoCover_diff}.

nodes.title: Sections extending to one piece vanish in the cokernel
nodes.statement:
For \(t \in \Gamma(X,U_0)\), the class of \(t|_{U_0 \cap U_1}\) in
  \ref{def:TwoCover_H1Cok} is zero; symmetrically, for \(t \in \Gamma(X,U_1)\) the class of
  \(t|_{U_0 \cap U_1}\) is zero.

nodes.title: The two-cover connecting map
nodes.statement:
Assume \(U_0 \cup U_1 = X\). The \(k\)-linear map
  \(\Gamma(X, U_0 \cap U_1) \to H^1(X, \struct{X/k})\): the connecting map
  \ref{def:moduleDelta} of the two-cover square (Definition~\ref{def:twoCoverSquare}) for
  \(F = \struct{X/k}\), followed by the inverse of the isomorphism
  \(H^1(X,\struct{X/k}) \cong H'^1(X,\struct{X/k})\) of
  \ref{def:HModule_linearEquivHModule'}.

nodes.title: The connecting class of a difference vanishes
nodes.statement: For \(t \in \Gamma(X,U_0) \times \Gamma(X,U_1)\), \(\mathrm{delta}(\mathrm{diff}(t)) = 0\).

nodes.title: The connecting class of an extending section vanishes
nodes.statement:
For \(t \in \Gamma(X,U_0)\), \(\mathrm{delta}(t|_{U_0 \cap U_1}) = 0\); symmetrically, for
  \(t \in \Gamma(X,U_1)\), \(\mathrm{delta}(t|_{U_0 \cap U_1}) = 0\).

nodes.title: Surjectivity of the two-cover connecting map
nodes.statement:
If \(U_0\) and \(U_1\) are affine opens of \(X\) (still with \(U_0 \cup U_1 = X\)), then
  \(\mathrm{delta} : \Gamma(X, U_0 \cap U_1) \to H^1(X,\struct{X/k})\) is surjective.

nodes.title: The two-affine-cover \(H^1\) cokernel bridge
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a commutative ring, \(X\) a scheme over \(\Spec k\), and \(U_0, U_1\) affine
  opens of \(X\) with \(U_0 \cup U_1 = X\). There is a \(k\)-linear isomorphism
  \[
    H^1\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr) \;\cong\; \Gamma(X, U_0 \cap U_1)\big/\mathrm{range}(\mathrm{diff}),
  \]
  where \(\mathrm{diff}(s_0,s_1) = s_0|_{U_0 \cap U_1} - s_1|_{U_0 \cap U_1}\)
  (\ref{def:TwoCover_diff}). No hypothesis on \(U_0 \cap U_1\) (affineness, separatedness, or
  even quasi-compactness) is needed: the derived Mayer--Vietoris sequence of
  \ref{thm:moduleShortComplex_shortExact} is exact regardless, and affineness of \(U_0, U_1\)
  alone kills their degree-one cohomology (\ref{thm:affine_open_h1_vanishing}); the classical
  hypothesis on the intersection is needed only for the \v{C}ech-complex identification of
  \(H^1\), which this route bypasses.

nodes.title: Compatibility with the connecting map
nodes.statement:
Under the isomorphism of \ref{thm:TwoCover_h1CokEquiv}, the class
  \(\mathrm{delta}(s)\) (Definition~\ref{def:TwoCover_delta}) corresponds, for every
  \(s \in \Gamma(X, U_0 \cap U_1)\), to the class of \(s\) in
  \(\Gamma(X,U_0 \cap U_1)/\mathrm{range}(\mathrm{diff})\).

nodes.title: Compatibility with the connecting map, inverse form
nodes.statement:
The inverse of the isomorphism of \ref{thm:TwoCover_h1CokEquiv} sends the class of
  \(s \in \Gamma(X, U_0 \cap U_1)\) to \(\mathrm{delta}(s)\).

nodes.title: Morphisms over the base intertwine the structure algebra maps
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a commutative ring, let \(X, Y\) be schemes over \(\Spec k\) and let
  \(\pi : X \to Y\) be a morphism compatible with the structure morphisms. For opens
  \(U \subseteq Y\) and \(V \subseteq X\) with \(V \subseteq \pi^{-1}(U)\), the two
  composite ring homomorphisms
  \[
    \Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \to \Gamma(Y, \top) \to \Gamma(Y, U)
      \xrightarrow{\ \pi^\sharp\ } \Gamma(X, V)
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \to \Gamma(X, \top) \to \Gamma(X, V)
  \]
  agree, where the unlabeled maps are induced by the structure morphisms and by
  restriction.

nodes.title: Pulling back the structure algebra map
nodes.statement:
In the situation of \ref{lem:appTop_map_appLE}, for every \(r \in k\) the map
  \(\pi^\sharp : \Gamma(Y, U) \to \Gamma(X, V)\) sends the image of \(r\) under the
  structure algebra map of \(Y\) (Definition~\ref{def:overAlgebraMap}) to the image of
  \(r\) under the structure algebra map of \(X\).

nodes.title: The basic-open models lie over the base
nodes.statement:
Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The composite of the affine
  model \(\Spec A_{(f)} \to \PP^1\) of the basic open \(D_+(f)\) with the structure
  morphism \(\PP^1 \to \Spec k\) is the morphism induced by the algebra map
  \(k \to A_{(f)}\). (This generalizes \ref{lem:P1_chartIota_structureMap} from the two
  standard charts to all standard basic opens.)

nodes.title: The basic-open inclusion factors through its affine model
nodes.statement:
Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The inclusion
  \(D_+(f) \to \PP^1\) is the composite of the canonical identification
  \(D_+(f) \cong \Spec A_{(f)}\) with the affine model \(\Spec A_{(f)} \to \PP^1\).

nodes.title: The structure algebra map on a basic open
nodes.statement:
Let \(f \in k[X_0, X_1]\) be homogeneous of positive degree. The composite
  \[
    \Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \to \Gamma(\PP^1, \top) \to \Gamma\bigl(\PP^1, D_+(f)\bigr)
  \]
  (structure morphism on global sections, then restriction) is the composite of the
  identification \(\Gamma(\Spec k, \top) \cong k\), the algebra map \(k \to A_{(f)}\), and
  the canonical map \(A_{(f)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(f))\).

nodes.title: The distinguished fraction of a chart pair is the chart coordinate
nodes.statement:
For \(i, j \in \{0,1\}\), the canonical degree-zero fraction
  \(X_j^{\deg X_i} / X_i^{\deg X_j}\) attached to the pair \((X_i, X_j)\) of homogeneous
  elements equals the chart coordinate \(t_{ij} = X_j / X_i \in A_{(X_i)}\).

nodes.title: The chart coordinate cuts out the overlap
nodes.statement:
For \(i, j \in \{0,1\}\), regard the chart coordinate \(t_{ij} \in A_{(X_i)}\) as a
  section of the structure sheaf over the chart \(U_i = D_+(X_i)\), via the canonical map
  \(A_{(X_i)} \to \Gamma(\PP^1, U_i)\). Then the basic open of this section in the scheme
  \(\PP^1\) --- the locus of \(U_i\) where it is invertible --- is the chart overlap:
  \[
    D(t_{ij}) \;=\; U_i \cap U_j .
  \]

nodes.title: The Laurent generators as restrictions from the charts
Finiteness of \(H^1\) along a finite morphism to the projective line
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a field, \(X\) a scheme over \(\Spec k\), and \(\pi : X \to \PP^1\) a
  finite morphism over \(k\) (its composite with the structure morphism of \(\PP^1\) is
  the structure morphism of \(X\)). Then \(H^1\bigl(X, \struct{X/k}\bigr)\) is a finite
  \(k\)-module.

nodes.title: Finiteness of \(H^1\) of the curve
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a field and \(C\) a smooth curve over \(k\) (proper, smooth of relative
  dimension one, geometrically irreducible). Then
  \(H^1\bigl(C, \struct{C/k}\bigr)\) is a finite \(k\)-module; equivalently, it is a
  finite-dimensional \(k\)-vector space.

nodes.title: The genus is the dimension of a finite-dimensional space
nodes.statement:
For a smooth curve \(C\) over \(k\), the genus of Definition~\ref{def:genus} is the
  \(k\)-dimension of \(H^1(C, \struct C)\), which by
  \ref{thm:moduleFinite_hModule_one} is a finite-dimensional \(k\)-vector space; the
  genus is therefore a well-defined natural number, attained as the cardinality of any
  basis.

nodes.title: Unramified flat algebras over a domain are reduced
nodes.statement:
Let \(B\) be an integral domain and let \(S\) be a commutative \(B\)-algebra which is
  formally unramified, essentially of finite type, and flat over \(B\). Then \(S\) is reduced.

nodes.title: \'Etale algebras over a domain are reduced
nodes.statement: An \'etale algebra over an integral domain is reduced.

nodes.title: Standard smooth homomorphisms out of a domain
nodes.statement:
Let \(B\) be an integral domain and let \(B \to S\) be a standard smooth ring homomorphism,
  that is, one admitting a presentation \(S = B[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\) in which the
  Jacobian matrix \((\partial f_u/\partial x_v)_{u,v \le c}\) has invertible determinant in
  \(S\). Then \(S\) is reduced.

nodes.title: Standard smooth algebras over a domain
nodes.statement: A standard smooth algebra over an integral domain is reduced.

nodes.title: Smooth schemes over a field are reduced
nodes.statement:
Let \(K\) be a field and let \(X\) be a scheme which is smooth over \(\Spec K\). Then \(X\)
  is reduced.

nodes.title: Smooth morphisms are geometrically reduced
nodes.statement:
A smooth morphism of schemes \(f : X \to Y\) is geometrically reduced: for every field \(K\)
  and every morphism \(\Spec K \to Y\), the base change \(X \times_Y \Spec K\) is a reduced
  scheme.

nodes.title: Smooth of relative dimension one implies smooth
nodes.statement: A morphism of schemes which is smooth of relative dimension one is smooth.

nodes.title: Smooth of a relative dimension implies geometrically reduced
nodes.statement:
For every \(n\), a morphism of schemes which is smooth of relative dimension \(n\) is
  geometrically reduced.

nodes.title: Smooth and geometrically irreducible implies geometrically integral
nodes.statement:
A smooth, geometrically irreducible morphism of schemes is geometrically integral: every
  base change to the spectrum of a field is an integral scheme.

nodes.title: Relative-dimension form
nodes.statement:
For every \(n\), a geometrically irreducible morphism of schemes which is smooth of relative
  dimension \(n\) is geometrically integral.

nodes.title: Irreducibility
nodes.statement:
If \(X\) is geometrically irreducible over \(k\), then the underlying topological space of
  \(X\) is irreducible; in particular \(X\) is nonempty.

nodes.title: Quasi-compactness
nodes.statement:
If \(X\) is quasi-compact over \(\Spec k\) (for instance proper), then the underlying
  topological space of \(X\) is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Quasi-separatedness
nodes.statement:
If \(X\) is quasi-separated over \(\Spec k\) (for instance proper), then the underlying
  topological space of \(X\) is quasi-separated: the intersection of any two quasi-compact
  opens is quasi-compact.

nodes.title: Integrality
nodes.statement:
If \(X\) is geometrically reduced and geometrically irreducible over \(k\), then \(X\) is an
  integral scheme.

nodes.title: Pushout of a field extension along itself
nodes.statement:
Let \(\varphi : A \to B\) and \(\psi : A \to C\) be homomorphisms of commutative rings with
  \(B\) nontrivial, and let \(D\), with coprojections \(\iota_B : B \to D\) and
  \(\iota_C : C \to D\), be a pushout of \((\varphi, \psi)\) (for instance
  \(D = B \otimes_A C\)). Assume that \(D\) is a field and that there is a ring isomorphism
  \(e : C \cong B\) with \(e \circ \psi = \varphi\). Then \(\varphi\) is an epimorphism in the
  category of commutative rings.

nodes.title: Global sections form a field
nodes.statement:
Let \(R\) be a commutative ring which is a field, let \(X\) be an integral scheme, and let
  \(f : X \to \Spec R\) be universally closed. Then \(\Gamma(X, \struct X)\) is a field.

nodes.title: Constant functions on a proper geometrically integral scheme
nodes.statement:
Let \(K\) be a field and let \(X\) be a scheme, proper and geometrically integral over
  \(K\). Then the ring homomorphism
  \(\Gamma(\Spec K, \struct{\Spec K}) \to \Gamma(X, \struct X)\) induced by the structure
  morphism is bijective; identifying \(\Gamma(\Spec K, \struct{\Spec K}) = K\), this says
  \(\Gamma(X, \struct X) = K\).

nodes.title: Isomorphism form
nodes.statement:
In the situation of \ref{thm:sections_k}, the induced map
  \(\Gamma(\Spec K, \struct{\Spec K}) \to \Gamma(X, \struct X)\) is an isomorphism of rings.

nodes.title: Global sections of the curve
nodes.statement:
Let \(C\) be a scheme over \(k\) which is proper, geometrically irreducible and
  geometrically reduced over \(k\). Then the structure morphism induces an isomorphism
  \(\Gamma(\Spec k, \struct{\Spec k}) \cong \Gamma(C, \struct C)\); that is,
  \(\Gamma(C, \struct C) = k\).

nodes.title: The smooth curve
nodes.statement:
Let \(C\) be a smooth curve over \(k\), i.e.\ proper, smooth of relative dimension one and
  geometrically irreducible over \(k\), as in Chapter~\ref{chap:Challenge}. Combining the
  above: \(C\) is smooth over \(k\) (\ref{lem:smooth_of_relDim_one}), geometrically reduced
  (\ref{lem:relDim_geometrically_reduced}) and geometrically integral
  (\ref{thm:relDim_geometrically_integral}); its underlying space is irreducible
  (\ref{lem:irreducible_of_geomirred}), quasi-compact (\ref{lem:curve_compact}) and
  quasi-separated (\ref{lem:curve_quasiseparated}); \(C\) is an integral scheme
  (\ref{prop:curve_integral}); and \(\Gamma(C, \struct C) = k\) (\ref{cor:curve_sections}).

nodes.title: The projective line
nodes.statement:
The projective line over \(k\) is \(\PP^1 = \Proj A\), the Proj of the graded ring
  \(A = k[X_0, X_1]\).

nodes.title: Degree zero
nodes.statement:
The inclusion of constants \(k \to A_0\) into the degree-zero part of \(A\) is an
  isomorphism of \(k\)-algebras.

nodes.title: Structure morphism
nodes.statement:
The structure morphism \(\PP^1 \to \Spec k\) is the canonical morphism
  \(\Proj A \to \Spec A_0\) followed by the isomorphism \(\Spec A_0 \cong \Spec k\) induced by
  \ref{def:P1_gradeZero}.

nodes.title: Properness of the projective line
nodes.statement: \(\PP^1\) is proper over \(k\).

nodes.title: The projective line as a scheme over \(k\)
nodes.statement:
\(\PP^1\), regarded as a scheme over \(k\) via the structure morphism of
  \ref{def:P1_structureMap}.

nodes.title: The standard charts
nodes.statement:
For \(i \in \{0,1\}\), the chart \(U_i = D_+(X_i) \subseteq \PP^1\) is the basic open locus
  where the homogeneous coordinate \(X_i\) does not vanish.

nodes.title: The charts are affine
nodes.statement: Each chart \(U_i\) is an affine open of \(\PP^1\).

nodes.title: Affine models of the charts
nodes.statement:
For \(i \in \{0,1\}\), the canonical morphism \(\Spec A_{(X_i)} \to \PP^1\) associated with
  the basic open at the degree-one element \(X_i\); it is an open immersion.

nodes.title: Image of the affine model
nodes.statement:
The image of \(\Spec A_{(X_i)} \to \PP^1\) is the chart \(U_i\); thus
  \(U_i \cong \Spec A_{(X_i)}\).

nodes.title: The affine models lie over \(k\)
nodes.statement:
The composite \(\Spec A_{(X_i)} \to \PP^1 \to \Spec k\) is the morphism induced by the
  \(k\)-algebra structure of \(A_{(X_i)}\); that is, the affine models are morphisms of
  schemes over \(k\).

nodes.title: Chart coordinates
nodes.statement:
For \(i, j \in \{0,1\}\), the chart coordinate is the degree-zero fraction
  \(t_{ij} = X_j / X_i \in A_{(X_i)}\).

nodes.title: Dehomogenization
nodes.statement:
For \(i \in \{0,1\}\), the dehomogenization at \(X_i\) is the \(k\)-algebra homomorphism
  \(\delta_i : k[X_0, X_1] \to k[t]\) with \(\delta_i(X_i) = 1\) and \(\delta_i(X_j) = t\) for
  \(j \neq i\).

nodes.title: From polynomials to the chart ring
nodes.statement:
For \(i, j \in \{0,1\}\), the \(k\)-algebra homomorphism \(k[t] \to A_{(X_i)}\) given by
  evaluation at the chart coordinate, \(t \mapsto t_{ij}\).

nodes.title: From the chart ring to polynomials
nodes.statement:
For \(i \in \{0,1\}\), the \(k\)-algebra homomorphism \(A_{(X_i)} \to k[t]\) sending a
  degree-zero fraction \(a / X_i^n\) (with \(a\) homogeneous of degree \(n\)) to
  \(\delta_i(a)\).

nodes.title: One composite is the identity
nodes.statement:
For \(i \neq j\), the composite \(k[t] \to A_{(X_i)} \to k[t]\) of
  \ref{def:P1_polyToAway} followed by \ref{def:P1_awayToPoly} is the identity.

nodes.title: Monomial fractions are powers of the coordinate
Surjectivity onto the chart ring
nodes.statement:
For \(i \neq j\), the homomorphism \(k[t] \to A_{(X_i)}\) of \ref{def:P1_polyToAway} is
  surjective.

nodes.title: The other composite is the identity
nodes.statement:
For \(i \neq j\), the composite \(A_{(X_i)} \to k[t] \to A_{(X_i)}\) of
  \ref{def:P1_awayToPoly} followed by \ref{def:P1_polyToAway} is the identity.

nodes.title: The chart identification
nodes.statement:
For \(i \neq j\), the isomorphism of \(k\)-algebras
  \(\alpha_i : A_{(X_i)} \cong k[t]\) given by the mutually inverse homomorphisms of
  \ref{def:P1_awayToPoly} and \ref{def:P1_polyToAway}; the chart coordinate \(t_{ij}\)
  corresponds to \(t\).

nodes.title: Laurent span
nodes.statement:
Every Laurent polynomial \(f \in R[T, T^{-1}]\) over a commutative (semi)ring \(R\) can be
  written as \(f = p(T) + q(T^{-1})\) with \(p, q \in R[t]\) ordinary polynomials.

nodes.title: Restriction from the left chart
nodes.statement:
The canonical ring homomorphism \(\lambda : A_{(X_0)} \to A_{(X_0 X_1)}\), sending
  \(a / X_0^{\,n}\) to \(a X_1^{\,n} / (X_0 X_1)^{n}\).

nodes.title: Restriction from the right chart
nodes.statement:
The canonical ring homomorphism \(\rho : A_{(X_1)} \to A_{(X_0 X_1)}\), sending
  \(a / X_1^{\,n}\) to \(a X_0^{\,n} / (X_0 X_1)^{n}\).

nodes.title: The two coordinates are mutually inverse on the overlap
nodes.statement: In \(A_{(X_0 X_1)}\) one has \(\lambda(t_{01}) \cdot \rho(t_{10}) = 1\).

nodes.title: The overlap ring is a localization of the chart ring
nodes.statement:
The homomorphism \(\lambda\) of \ref{def:P1_awayToOverlapLeft} identifies
  \(A_{(X_0 X_1)}\) with the localization of \(A_{(X_0)}\) at the powers of the chart
  coordinate \(t_{01}\).

nodes.title: The overlap identification
nodes.statement:
The isomorphism of \(k\)-algebras \(\theta : A_{(X_0 X_1)} \cong k[T, T^{-1}]\), with
  \(T\) the image of the coordinate \(t_{01}\).

nodes.title: Left restriction is \(t \mapsto T\)
nodes.statement:
For every \(z \in A_{(X_0)}\) one has \(\theta(\lambda(z)) = p(T)\), where
  \(p = \alpha_0(z) \in k[t]\). In other words, under the identifications
  \(\alpha_0\) and \(\theta\), the restriction \(\lambda\) is the canonical inclusion
  \(k[t] \to k[T, T^{-1}]\), \(t \mapsto T\).

nodes.title: Right restriction is \(t \mapsto T^{-1}\)
nodes.statement:
For every \(z \in A_{(X_1)}\) one has \(\theta(\rho(z)) = q(T^{-1})\), where
  \(q = \alpha_1(z) \in k[t]\). In other words, under the identifications \(\alpha_1\) and
  \(\theta\), the restriction \(\rho\) is the homomorphism \(k[t] \to k[T, T^{-1}]\),
  \(t \mapsto T^{-1}\).

nodes.title: Laurent span on the overlap ring
nodes.statement:
Every \(w \in A_{(X_0 X_1)}\) can be written as \(w = \lambda(z_0) + \rho(z_1)\) with
  \(z_0 \in A_{(X_0)}\) and \(z_1 \in A_{(X_1)}\).

nodes.title: The overlap is affine
nodes.statement: The chart overlap \(U_0 \cap U_1 = D_+(X_0 X_1)\) is an affine open of \(\PP^1\).

nodes.title: Sections on the left chart
nodes.statement:
The ring isomorphism \(\gamma_0 : \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0) \cong k[t]\): the canonical
  identification \(\Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(X_0)) \cong A_{(X_0)}\) (sections of \(\Proj\) over a
  basic open; equivalently, \(U_0 = \Spec A_{(X_0)}\) via \ref{def:P1_chartIota}) followed by
  \(\alpha_0\) of \ref{def:P1_awayAlgEquiv}.

nodes.title: Sections on the right chart
nodes.statement:
The ring isomorphism \(\gamma_1 : \Gamma(\PP^1, U_1) \cong k[t]\), defined as in
  \ref{def:P1_chartSectionsEquiv0} with the identification
  \(\Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(X_1)) \cong A_{(X_1)}\) followed by \(\alpha_1\).

nodes.title: Sections on the overlap
nodes.statement:
The ring isomorphism \(\gamma_{01} : \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0 \cap U_1) \cong k[T, T^{-1}]\): the
  canonical identification \(\Gamma(\PP^1, D_+(X_0X_1)) \cong A_{(X_0X_1)}\) followed by
  \(\theta\) of \ref{def:P1_overlapAlgEquiv}.

nodes.title: Restriction of sections from the left chart
nodes.statement:
For every section \(a \in \Gamma(\PP^1, U_0)\),
  \[
    \gamma_{01}\bigl(a|_{U_0 \cap U_1}\bigr) = p(T), \qquad p = \gamma_0(a);
  \]
  under the identifications, restriction from the left chart to the overlap is
  \(t \mapsto T\).

nodes.title: Restriction of sections from the right chart
nodes.statement:
For every section \(b \in \Gamma(\PP^1, U_1)\),
  \[
    \gamma_{01}\bigl(b|_{U_0 \cap U_1}\bigr) = q(T^{-1}), \qquad q = \gamma_1(b);
  \]
  under the identifications, restriction from the right chart to the overlap is
  \(t \mapsto T^{-1}\).

nodes.title: Laurent chart pair
nodes.statement:
A \emph{Laurent chart pair} on \(\PP^1\) consists of open subsets
  \(V_0, V_1, V_{01} \subseteq \PP^1\) with \(V_{01} \subseteq V_0\),
  \(V_{01} \subseteq V_1\) and \(V_0 \cap V_1 = V_{01}\), all three affine, covering the
  projective line (\(V_0 \cup V_1 = \PP^1\)), together with ring isomorphisms
  \[
    \Gamma_0 : \Gamma(\PP^1, V_0) \cong k[t], \quad
    \Gamma_1 : \Gamma(\PP^1, V_1) \cong k[t], \quad
    \Gamma_{01} : \Gamma(\PP^1, V_{01}) \cong k[T, T^{-1}],
  \]
  such that, under these identifications, restriction \(V_{01} \subseteq V_0\) is
  \(t \mapsto T\) and restriction \(V_{01} \subseteq V_1\) is \(t \mapsto T^{-1}\).

nodes.title: Laurent span for a chart pair
nodes.statement:
Let \((V_0, V_1, V_{01}, \Gamma_0, \Gamma_1, \Gamma_{01})\) be a Laurent chart pair on
  \(\PP^1\). Every section \(z \in \Gamma(\PP^1, V_{01})\) is the sum of a restriction from
  \(V_0\) and a restriction from \(V_1\): there are \(a \in \Gamma(\PP^1, V_0)\) and
  \(b \in \Gamma(\PP^1, V_1)\) with \(z = a|_{V_{01}} + b|_{V_{01}}\).

nodes.title: The canonical Laurent chart pair
nodes.statement:
The Laurent chart pair on \(\PP^1\) given by the standard charts: \(V_0 = U_0\),
  \(V_1 = U_1\), \(V_{01} = D_+(X_0X_1)\), with the identifications \(\gamma_0, \gamma_1,
  \gamma_{01}\) of \ref{def:P1_chartSectionsEquiv0}--\ref{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv}.

nodes.title: Unramified finite-type domains over a Dedekind domain, DVR form
nodes.statement:
Let \(A\) be a Dedekind domain and \(B\) an integral domain which is an \(A\)-algebra of
  finite type and formally unramified over \(A\). Then \(B\) is Noetherian, and the
  localization of \(B\) at every nonzero prime ideal is a discrete valuation ring.

nodes.title: Unramified finite-type domains over a Dedekind domain
nodes.statement:
Let \(A\) be a Dedekind domain and \(B\) an integral domain which is an \(A\)-algebra of
  finite type and formally unramified over \(A\). Then \(B\) is a Dedekind domain.

nodes.title: The polynomial ring in one variable is a principal ideal ring
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a field. The polynomial ring over \(k\) on a one-element set of variables is
  a principal ideal ring.

nodes.title: The polynomial ring in one variable is Dedekind
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a field. The polynomial ring over \(k\) on a one-element set of variables is
  a Dedekind domain.

nodes.title: Structure theorem for standard smooth algebras
nodes.statement:
\textit{Provided by Mathlib.}
  Let \(R\) be a commutative ring and \(S\) an \(R\)-algebra which is standard smooth of
  relative dimension \(n\): it admits a presentation
  \(S = R[x_1,\dots,x_m]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\) with \(m - c = n\) in which the Jacobian matrix
  \((\partial f_u/\partial x_v)_{u,v \le c}\) has invertible determinant in \(S\). Then the
  structure map factors as
  \[
    R \longrightarrow R[y_1, \dots, y_n] \longrightarrow S
  \]
  with the second homomorphism \'etale. (For such a presentation the module of K\"ahler
  differentials \(\Omega_{S/R}\) is free on the images of
  \(dx_{c+1}, \dots, dx_m\); consequently \(S\) is unramified, hence \'etale, over the
  polynomial subring on those last \(n\) coordinates.)

nodes.title: Standard smooth domains of relative dimension one are Dedekind
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a field and \(B\) an integral domain which is a standard smooth
  \(k\)-algebra of relative dimension \(1\). Then \(B\) is a Dedekind domain.

nodes.title: Standard smooth algebras of relative dimension one contain a transcendental
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a field and \(B\) a nontrivial standard smooth \(k\)-algebra of relative
  dimension \(1\). Then \(B\) contains an element transcendental over \(k\).

nodes.title: Stalks over Dedekind section rings are valuation rings
nodes.statement:
Let \(X\) be an integral scheme, \(V \subseteq X\) an affine open whose ring of sections
  \(\Gamma(X, V)\) is a Dedekind domain, and \(x \in V\). Then the stalk
  \(\struct{X,x}\) is a valuation ring.

nodes.title: Height-one specialization over Dedekind section rings
nodes.statement:
Let \(X\) be a scheme whose underlying space is irreducible, \(V \subseteq X\) an affine
  open with \(\Gamma(X, V)\) a Dedekind domain, and \(x \in V\). Then every generalization
  of \(x\) is the generic point of \(X\) or \(x\) itself.

nodes.title: Non-generic points are closed
nodes.statement:
Let \(X\) be a scheme whose underlying space is irreducible and whose specialization
  order has height one: every generalization of any point is the generic point or the
  point itself. Then every point other than the generic point is closed.

nodes.title: Finiteness of proper closed subsets
nodes.statement:
Let \(X\) be a scheme whose underlying space is irreducible and Noetherian and whose
  specialization order has height one. Then every closed subset \(Z \subseteq X\) not
  containing the generic point is finite.

nodes.title: Dedekind charts on a curve
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a field and \(X\) an integral scheme, smooth of relative dimension one over
  \(\Spec k\). Then every point of \(X\) lies in an affine open \(V\) whose ring of
  sections \(\Gamma(X, V)\) is a Dedekind domain.

nodes.title: The stalks of a curve are valuation rings
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a field and \(X\) an integral scheme, smooth of relative dimension one over
  \(\Spec k\). Then every stalk of the structure sheaf of \(X\) is a valuation ring.

nodes.title: Height-one specialization on a curve
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a field and \(X\) an integral scheme, smooth of relative dimension one over
  \(\Spec k\). Then every generalization of a point of \(X\) is the generic point or the
  point itself.

nodes.title: Existence of a transcendental rational function
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a field and \(X\) an integral scheme, smooth of relative dimension one over
  \(\Spec k\). Regard the function field \(K(X)\) --- the stalk of the structure sheaf at
  the generic point --- as a ring under \(k\) via the structure morphism (global sections
  followed by the germ at the generic point). Then \(K(X)\) contains an element \(f_0\)
  transcendental over \(k\): no nonzero polynomial with coefficients in \(k\) vanishes at
  \(f_0\).

nodes.title: The chart models are domains
nodes.statement:
The chart rings \(A_{(X_0)}\) and \(A_{(X_1)}\) are integral domains, and the overlap
  ring \(A_{(X_0X_1)}\) is nontrivial.

nodes.title: The chart section rings are principal ideal rings
nodes.statement: For \(i \in \{0,1\}\), the ring \(\Gamma(\PP^1, U_i)\) is a principal ideal ring.

nodes.title: The chart section rings are domains
nodes.statement: For \(i \in \{0,1\}\), the ring \(\Gamma(\PP^1, U_i)\) is an integral domain.

nodes.title: The chart section rings are Dedekind
nodes.statement: For \(i \in \{0,1\}\), the ring \(\Gamma(\PP^1, U_i)\) is a Dedekind domain.

nodes.title: Every nonempty open meets the left chart
nodes.statement: Every nonempty open subset \(W \subseteq \PP^1\) contains a point of the chart \(U_0\).

nodes.title: Irreducibility of the projective line
nodes.statement: The underlying topological space of \(\PP^1\) is irreducible (in particular nonempty).

nodes.title: The generic point through the chart
nodes.statement:
The affine model \(\Spec A_{(X_0)} \to \PP^1\) sends the generic point of
  \(\Spec A_{(X_0)}\) to the generic point of \(\PP^1\).

nodes.title: A second point of the projective line
nodes.statement: \(\PP^1\) has a point distinct from its generic point.

nodes.title: Height-one specialization on the projective line
nodes.statement: Every generalization of a point of \(\PP^1\) is the generic point or the point itself.

nodes.title: Non-generic points of the projective line are closed
nodes.statement: Every point of \(\PP^1\) other than the generic point is closed.

nodes.title: Separatedness of the projective line
nodes.statement: \(\PP^1\) is a separated scheme.

nodes.title: Evaluation of the chart ring
nodes.statement:
Let \(A\) be a commutative ring under \(k\), i.e.\ equipped with a ring homomorphism
  \(\sigma : k \to A\), let \(i \in \{0,1\}\) and \(a \in A\). The evaluation of the chart
  ring at \(a\) is the ring homomorphism
  \[
    A_{(X_i)} \longrightarrow A, \qquad
    z \longmapsto \bigl(\text{the polynomial } \alpha_i(z) \in k[t]\bigr)
      \text{ evaluated at } t = a \text{ with coefficients mapped by } \sigma
  \]
  (composite of \ref{def:P1_awayToPoly} with polynomial evaluation). It sends the chart
  coordinate \(t_{ij}\) (\(j \neq i\)) to \(a\) and a constant \(c \in k\) to \(\sigma(c)\).

nodes.title: Morphisms to the projective line through a chart
nodes.statement:
With \(\sigma : k \to A\), \(i \in \{0,1\}\) and \(a \in A\) as in
  \ref{def:P1_chartEval}: the morphism \(\Spec A \to \PP^1\) obtained by applying
  \(\Spec\) to the evaluation \(A_{(X_i)} \to A\) at \(a\) and composing with the affine
  model \(\Spec A_{(X_i)} \to \PP^1\) of \ref{def:P1_chartIota}. For \(i = 0\) this is the
  ``point'' \([1 : a]\); for \(i = 1\) it is \([a : 1]\).

nodes.title: The chart morphisms lie over the base
nodes.statement:
The composite of the morphism of \ref{def:P1_fromSpecChart} with the structure morphism
  \(\PP^1 \to \Spec k\) is \(\Spec \sigma : \Spec A \to \Spec k\).

nodes.title: Naturality of the chart morphisms
nodes.statement:
Let \(g : A \to A'\) be a homomorphism of rings under \(k\) (so \(A'\) is under \(k\)
  via \(g \circ \sigma\)), \(i \in \{0,1\}\) and \(a \in A\). Then the composite
  \(\Spec A' \xrightarrow{\Spec g} \Spec A \to \PP^1\) of \ref{def:P1_fromSpecChart} at
  \(a\) is the morphism of \ref{def:P1_fromSpecChart} at \(g(a) \in A'\).

nodes.title: The chart restrictions factor the overlap model
nodes.statement:
Applying \(\Spec\) to the restriction homomorphism \(\lambda : A_{(X_0)} \to
  A_{(X_0X_1)}\) (resp.\ \(\rho : A_{(X_1)} \to A_{(X_0X_1)}\)) of
  \ref{def:P1_awayToOverlapLeft} (resp.\ \ref{def:P1_awayToOverlapRight}) and composing
  with the affine model of the chart \(U_0\) (resp.\ \(U_1\)) yields the affine model
  \(\Spec A_{(X_0X_1)} \to \PP^1\) of the overlap \(D_+(X_0X_1)\).

nodes.title: The gluing identity
nodes.statement:
Let \(\sigma : k \to A\) and let \(u \in A\) be a unit. Then the morphism
  \([1 : u] : \Spec A \to \PP^1\) through the chart \(U_0\) equals the morphism
  \([u^{-1} : 1]\) through the chart \(U_1\) (both as in \ref{def:P1_fromSpecChart}).

nodes.title: Transcendental points land on the generic point
nodes.statement:
Let \(A\) be an integral domain under \(\sigma : k \to A\) and let \(a \in A\) be
  transcendental in the sense that no nonzero polynomial over \(k\), evaluated at \(a\)
  with coefficients mapped by \(\sigma\), vanishes. Then the morphism
  \([1 : a] : \Spec A \to \PP^1\) of \ref{def:P1_fromSpecChart} sends the generic point of
  \(\Spec A\) to the generic point of \(\PP^1\).

nodes.title: Stalk morphisms are compatible with specialization
nodes.statement:
Let \(X\) be a scheme, \(U \subseteq X\) open, \(x \in U\), and let \(y\) be a
  generalization of \(x\) (so \(y \in U\) as well). Write
  \(\struct{X,x} \to \struct{X,y}\) for the canonical map of stalks (restriction of
  germs). Then the composite
  \[
    \Spec \struct{X,y} \longrightarrow \Spec \struct{X,x} \longrightarrow U
  \]
  of the induced morphism of spectra with the canonical morphism
  \(\Spec \struct{X,x} \to U\) is the canonical morphism \(\Spec \struct{X,y} \to U\).

nodes.title: Partial and rational maps
nodes.statement:
\textit{Provided by Mathlib.}
  Let \(X, Y\) be schemes over a base \(S\). A \emph{partial map} \(X \dashrightarrow Y\)
  is a morphism to \(Y\) from a dense open subscheme of \(X\) (its \emph{domain}); a
  \emph{rational map} is an equivalence class of partial maps, two being equivalent when
  they agree on a common dense open. For \(X\) irreducible with generic point \(\xi\) and
  function field \(K(X) = \struct{X,\xi}\), a partial map \(g\) restricts to a morphism
  \(\Spec K(X) \to Y\) (its \emph{function-field morphism}), which determines the rational
  map. For \(X\) integral and \(Y\) locally of finite type over \(S\):
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item every \(S\)-morphism \(\Spec K(X) \to Y\) arises as the function-field morphism
      of a unique rational \(S\)-map \(X \dashrightarrow Y\) (spreading out);
    \item if moreover an \(S\)-morphism \(\Spec \struct{X,x} \to Y\) restricting to the
      given one on \(\Spec K(X)\) exists at a point \(x\), then \(x\) lies in the domain
      of definition of that rational map (the union of the domains of its
      representatives);
    \item if \(Y\) is separated, a rational map has a largest representative, defined on
      its whole domain of definition.
  \end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Restriction of a partial map to the function field
nodes.statement:
Let \(X\) be a scheme with irreducible underlying space, \(g : X \dashrightarrow Y\) a
  partial map and \(x\) a point of its domain. Then the function-field morphism of \(g\)
  is the composite
  \[
    \Spec K(X) \longrightarrow \Spec \struct{X,x}
      \longrightarrow Y,
  \]
  where the first arrow is induced by the canonical map
  \(\struct{X,x} \to K(X) = \struct{X,\xi}\) and the second is the restriction of \(g\) to
  \(\Spec \struct{X,x}\).

nodes.title: The structure map of a stalk
nodes.statement:
Let \(f : X \to \Spec k\) be a scheme over \(k\) and \(x \in X\). The structure map of
  the stalk at \(x\) is the composite ring homomorphism
  \(k \to \Gamma(X, X) \to \struct{X,x}\) of the map induced by \(f\) on global sections
  with the germ at \(x\); it makes every stalk of \(X\) a ring under \(k\).

nodes.title: Coherence of the structure maps of stalks
nodes.statement:
Let \(f : X \to \Spec k\) and \(x \in X\).
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item Applying \(\Spec\) to the structure map of \ref{def:structureStalk} yields the
      composite \(\Spec \struct{X,x} \to X \xrightarrow{f} \Spec k\) of the canonical
      morphism with \(f\).
    \item For a generalization \(y\) of \(x\), composing the structure map at \(x\) with
      the canonical map \(\struct{X,x} \to \struct{X,y}\) yields the structure map at
      \(y\).
  \end{enumerate}

nodes.title: A smooth projective curve maps locally quasi-finitely to the line
nodes.statement:
Let \(X\) be an integral scheme, proper and smooth of relative dimension one over the
  field \(k\). Then there is a morphism \(\pi : X \to \PP^1\) over \(k\) which is locally
  quasi-finite.

nodes.title: Zariski's main theorem, cancellation form
nodes.statement:
Let \(\pi : X \to Y\) and \(g : Y \to S\) be morphisms of schemes with \(\pi\) locally
  quasi-finite, \(g\) separated and \(g \circ \pi\) proper. Then \(\pi\) is finite.

nodes.title: Locally quasi-finite maps to the projective line are finite
nodes.statement:
Let \(X\) be a scheme, proper over \(k\), and let \(\pi : X \to \PP^1\) be a locally
  quasi-finite morphism over \(k\) (i.e.\ its composite with the structure morphism of
  \(\PP^1\) is the structure morphism of \(X\)). Then \(\pi\) is finite.

nodes.title: Reduction to local quasi-finiteness
nodes.statement:
Let \(C\) be a scheme, proper over \(k\). If there exists a locally quasi-finite morphism
  \(C \to \PP^1\) over \(k\), then there exists a finite morphism \(C \to \PP^1\) over \(k\).

nodes.title: Existence of a finite morphism to the projective line
nodes.statement:
Let \(C\) be a smooth curve over \(k\) (proper, smooth of relative dimension one,
  geometrically irreducible). Then there exists a finite morphism \(\pi : C \to \PP^1\) over
  \(k\).

nodes.title: Preimages of the charts are affine
nodes.statement:
Let \(\pi : Y \to \PP^1\) be an affine morphism (for instance a finite one). Then
  \(\pi^{-1}(U_i)\) is an affine open of \(Y\) for \(i \in \{0,1\}\).

nodes.title: Preimages of the charts cover
nodes.statement:
For any morphism \(\pi : Y \to \PP^1\), the preimages of the two standard charts cover
  \(Y\): \(\pi^{-1}(U_0) \cup \pi^{-1}(U_1) = Y\).

nodes.title: Module-finiteness over the charts
nodes.statement:
Let \(\pi : Y \to \PP^1\) be a finite morphism. For \(i \in \{0,1\}\), the induced ring
  homomorphism \(\Gamma(\PP^1, U_i) \to \Gamma(Y, \pi^{-1}(U_i))\) is module-finite. (By
  \ref{def:P1_chartSectionsEquiv0}--\ref{def:P1_chartSectionsEquiv1}, the source is the
  polynomial ring \(k[t]\).)

nodes.title: Module-finiteness over the overlap
nodes.statement:
Let \(\pi : Y \to \PP^1\) be a finite morphism. The induced ring homomorphism
  \(\Gamma(\PP^1, U_0 \cap U_1) \to \Gamma(Y, \pi^{-1}(U_0 \cap U_1))\) is module-finite.
  (By \ref{def:P1_overlapSectionsEquiv}, the source is the Laurent polynomial ring
  \(k[T,T^{-1}]\).)
